fact: The Transition government's PMO/PGE-R programme says the Government will continue the digitalisation of the electoral roll and of the election process, including digital security of the roll.

Newsmada reports that a UNDP tender this year covers servers and computers for CENI's management of biometric data, and that CENI received USD 750,000 of Japan-UNDP IT equipment on 23 October 2026 in preparation for a biometric voter list; the current overhaul still runs on an alphanumeric system, with over 7.16 million registered against a 14 million target.

Madagascar's electoral commission (Ceni) will collect voter data mainly on paper forms for the roll overhaul due in August 2026, with tablets in a limited number of centres only; the article says digitalisation is not yet in place.

L'Express de Madagascar reports that the August 2026 overhaul of the voters' roll will rely mainly on paper voter information forms with tablets in only a few centres, and an electoral agent says no digitalisation is planned.
